```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B's demand evidence includes people already spending to solve the problem. One quote says \"I hired someone. It costs a lot,\" and another puts the cost at 3-4 hours every month. A's quotes show anxiety about gaps but no spending.",
    "B's need recurs every month and supports a $29-100/mo price anchored to two competitors with published pricing (Kick, FlexedLedger). A's need ends at re-employment, its price is $8-24/mo, and its buyers are often financially strained. That makes a first paid conversion and its payback harder.",
    "B has a sourced, low-cost route to buyers: the Stripe App Marketplace reaches Stripe's existing users for only dev and review time. A relies mainly on paid ads with a sourced Google cost per lead of roughly $63-118 (Meta about $12) and a conversion rate the brief itself calls unverified.",
    "Both niches are crowded and both briefs admit it. A's competitors include free tools such as GapZero, and its own demand quote shows users substituting a ChatGPT subscription they already pay for. That makes paying for a narrow gap-framing tool less likely.",
    "B's risks are real: six or more competitors with free tiers, expectations of SOC2 security audits, and finance clicks that can exceed $50. The brief's own suggestion of narrowing to pure Stripe-to-bank reconciliation, sold through the Stripe marketplace, is a plausible path to one paying customer within 90 days."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's demand evidence does not show willingness to pay. The forum quotes describe fear of resume gaps, not paying for a fix. The one quote about spending (\"I don't have $100–$150 per hour... but I do have a subscription to ChatGPT\") suggests users will use a general AI tool they already have rather than buy a new one. CoachGPT's pricing is NOT FOUND, ResAlign's is unpublished, and the free-to-paid conversion rate the paid-ads math depends on is explicitly unverified.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Both briefs describe saturated niches with free competitors and no clear differentiation, so neither is strong. B also has gaps: the Growthy estimate of $400-600/mo in bookkeeper time has no source link, the privacy-law details are marked [unsourced], and the free tiers may already cover low-volume solo founders. B wins on recurring spend, higher price, and a free distribution channel, not on clean evidence."
}
```
